Stellar Scaffold · HackMeridian 2026

From idea to working dApp, fast.

A toolkit for full-stack Stellar apps. One command gives you Rust smart contracts, a React or Svelte frontend, a local network, and typed TypeScript clients that rebuild every time your contract changes.

Docsstellarscaffold.org Codegithub.com/stellar-scaffold Registryrgstry.xyz
Same first line as the handout they're holding. One command: contracts, frontend, local network, typed clients. ~30s.

The hackathon problem

  • Build Rust → Wasm
  • Deploy, copy the contract ID
  • Generate bindings, paste the ID into the frontend
  • Wire up a wallet and network config
  • …then change one function and do it all again
This plumbing eats the first day of a hackathon. Scaffold makes it one loop. ~30s.

Three things to remember

scaffold.yml = your dependencies

Your app's contract dependencies, per network: what they are and where to get them.

Secrets and machine settings go in .env.

app-lib/clients = generated

A typed client per contract, per network, regenerated on every build and gitignored. Import by name; never paste an address.

Don't edit it: wrap clients under app/.

npm run dev = the loop

Save a contract and it rebuilds, redeploys on the local network, and regenerates its client.

App runs at localhost:5173.

These are the three boxes at the top of the handout. ~45s.

1–2Set up and start a project


cargo install --locked \
  stellar-scaffold-cli stellar-registry-cli
stellar scaffold doctor   # checks your setup
stellar scaffold init my-app   # template + package manager
cd my-app && npm install && npm run dev
    

my-app/
├── contracts/     Rust → Wasm
├── app/           your frontend
├── app-lib/       wallet, network
│   └── clients/   generated
├── scaffold.yml   dependencies
└── .env           local settings

Needs Rust, Node, the Stellar CLI, and Docker. Scaffold and Registry install together as stellar plugins.

Sections 1 and 2 of the handout. Install Registry alongside Scaffold: it's how you get to testnet later. Skip prompts with --template react|svelte|none, -p <package-manager>, -y. ~40s.

Your frontend: React or Svelte

Pick one at init. Both templates ship wallet connect, network switching, and a working GuessTheNumber component, all using the same generated clients.


import { guessTheNumber } from "@stellar-scaffold/app-lib/clients"   // both
React · GuessTheNumber.tsx

const { address, signTransaction } =
  useWallet()
const tx = await guessTheNumber.guess(
  { a_number: 5n, guesser: address },
  { publicKey: address },
)
await tx.signAndSend({ signTransaction })
Svelte · GuessTheNumber.svelte

import { address, signTransaction }
  from "../stores/wallet"

const tx = await guessTheNumber.guess(
  { a_number: 5n, guesser: $address },
  { publicKey: $address },
)
await tx.signAndSend({ signTransaction })

Prefer your own UI? --template none still gives you app-lib and the clients.

Same client call, two frameworks: React uses the useWallet hook, Svelte uses a wallet store. The contract client is identical, so switching networks needs no code change. ~40s.

Live demo

Save → redeploy → typed client


/// Is the answer higher or lower than your guess?
pub fn hint(env: &Env, a_number: u64) -> Symbol {
    let n = Self::number(env);
    if a_number < n {
        symbol_short!("higher")
    } else if a_number > n {
        symbol_short!("lower")
    } else { symbol_short!("yes") }
}
    

const { result } = await guessTheNumber.hint({ a_number: 5n })
Pre-built app is already running (npm run dev). Paste hint() into contracts/guess-the-number/src/lib.rs, save. Point at watcher output: build, redeploy, client regenerated. In GuessTheNumber.tsx type "guessTheNumber." and show hint in autocomplete. If anything stalls >15s, press ↓ for the recording. ~2 min.

3Add a contract


stellar scaffold generate contract --from oz/nft-royalties   # or --from-wizard
  

contracts:
  my-nft:                   # client name; exported as myNft
    type: workspace         # built from contracts/, deployed locally
    source: nft-royalties   # crate name in its Cargo.toml
    args:                   # constructor args, by parameter name
      owner: ${account.me}
    networks:               # where your app uses this contract
      local:

generate writes the crate but does not add it to scaffold.yml; do that yourself.

Handout section 3. Start from vetted OpenZeppelin examples; --ls lists them. ~40s.

5Go to testnet and ship

Scaffold only deploys locally. Testnet contracts go through Stellar Registry; scaffold.yml just points at them.


contracts:
  my-nft:
    networks:
      local:              # built from contracts/
      testnet:
        type: contract    # already deployed: fetch it
        source: C...      # ID from registry
    

stellar scaffold build --compile-only
stellar registry publish ...  # next talk
stellar registry deploy ...
stellar scaffold build --network testnet
npm run build                 # → dist/

Set STELLAR_NETWORK=testnet in .env. Contracts can differ between networks: make sure the app still typechecks.

Handout section 5. Big change from older Scaffold: no allow-deploy, no testnet deploys from Scaffold. Build the Wasm, publish and deploy it with Registry (that's the next talk), then point scaffold.yml's testnet entry at the deployed ID. build --network testnet fetches it and regenerates the clients. ~40s.

7–8Hackathon survival kit

  • stellar scaffold doctor: anything broken, with a fix
  • stellar scaffold clean: changed constructor args? Start fresh
  • Works locally, breaks on testnet? Rebuild with --network testnet and fix type errors
  • Find contracts to depend on at rgstry.xyz
  • Teach your agent: Scaffold skill at skills.stellar.org
Handout sections 7 and 8. Everything is on the sheet. ~25s.

Your contract works locally.
How do you get it onto testnet under a name,
and use other people's without copying addresses?


stellar registry publish …   # under unverified/
Hand off to Registry here. ~10s.

Stellar Registry · HackMeridian 2026

Name it. Publish it. Import it.

Scaffold runs your contract locally. The registry is how it gets to testnet: publish the Wasm, deploy it under a name, and anyone, your own app included, uses that name instead of a C… address.

Docsstellarscaffold.org/docs/registry Codegithub.com/stellar-registry Explorerrgstry.xyz
Answer the last Scaffold slide: your contract works locally, Scaffold won't deploy it to testnet, the registry does. And once it has a name, other people can find it and you can use theirs the same way. Same headline as the handout. ~45s.

Three things to remember

Wasm = published code

Reusable contract code under a name and a semantic version. Only its author can publish new versions.

unverified/guess-the-number@1.0.0

Contract = deployed instance

A live contract registered by name. The name resolves to its C… address.

No version: it's one address.

unverified/ = open to all

Anyone can publish here, no approval. Bare names on the main registry need a manager's OK.

Use it this weekend.

The three boxes at the top of the Registry handout. Same shape as Scaffold's three things. The unverified/ prefix is the one thing that trips people up. ~1 min.

Ship to testnet by name


stellar keys fund me --network testnet
stellar keys use me

stellar registry publish \
  --wasm target/stellar/testnet/guess_the_number.wasm \
  --wasm-name unverified/guess-the-number --binver 1.0.0

stellar registry deploy \
  --contract-name unverified/guess-the-number \
  --wasm-name unverified/guess-the-number --version 1.0.0 \
  -- --admin me                        # constructor args after --

stellar registry fetch-contract-id unverified/guess-the-number   # C… for scaffold.yml

The Wasm is what stellar scaffold build --compile-only wrote with STELLAR_NETWORK=testnet. Add --dry-run to preview any write.

These are the two "next talk" lines from Scaffold's ship slide. Fund the testnet account and make it the default. Publish the Wasm Scaffold compiled under a name and version. Deploy a named instance from it; constructor args go after --. Then fetch the C… address: that's what goes in scaffold.yml next. CLI users can also run create-alias and invoke it by name. ~1:45.

Today works now

    networks:
      local:              # built from contracts/
      testnet:
        type: contract    # already deployed: fetch it
        source: C...      # from fetch-contract-id
By name coming soon

  guess-the-number:
    networks:
      local:              # built from contracts/
      testnet:
        type: registry    # resolve the name
        source: unverified/guess-the-number

Tracked in stellar-scaffold/cli#617.

Then stellar scaffold build --network testnet regenerates the typed guessTheNumber client against testnet. Same for anyone else's contract.

The same per-network entry as Scaffold's ship slide, filled in. local still builds from contracts/; testnet points at the deployed contract. Today you paste the C… address from fetch-contract-id. Coming soon: the registry name goes straight into scaffold.yml (cli#617). If #617 ships before the event, drop the left column. ~1:30.

Use theirs from Rust

You already have: guess-the-number pays out with stellar_registry::import_asset!("xlm").


let game = stellar_registry::import_contract!(
    env, "unverified/guess-the-number");   // typed client, no address in source

let won = game.guess(&5, &player);
  

STELLAR_NETWORK=testnet stellar scaffold build   # names resolve at build time

Defaults to local. The address is baked in: after a redeploy, cargo clean and rebuild.

The template contract already uses the registry for XLM (contracts/guess-the-number/src/xlm.rs). import_contract! turns a name into a client bound to its address, built from the on-chain Wasm. Set STELLAR_NETWORK=testnet in .env, as on Scaffold's ship slide. Short on time: show only the import_contract! line. ~1:15.

Find contracts, ship new versions

Depend on someone else's

Browse rgstry.xyz (and testnet.rgstry.xyz) for published Wasms and named contracts, then add one to scaffold.yml or import_contract! it by name.

Ship a new version of yours

stellar registry publish … --binver 1.1.0
stellar registry upgrade \
  --contract-name unverified/guess-the-number \
  --wasm-name unverified/guess-the-number

Upgrade calls the contract's own upgrade, so its admin signs. Same name, same address.

Cut this slide if over 13:00. Matches the "Handy extras" tip on the Scaffold handout: browse rgstry.xyz for contracts to depend on. Upgrade uses the latest published version unless --version is given; the address doesn't change, so scaffold.yml doesn't either. ~30s.

Registry survival kit

  • Auth failure on publish? You used a bare name. Add unverified/
  • Error(Contract, #5): that contract name is taken. #8: publish a higher --binver
  • Macro can't find a contract? STELLAR_NETWORK wasn't set at build time
  • deploy … -- --help prints the constructor's arguments
  • Teach your agent: Registry skill at skills.stellar.org
The "Common errors" box on the back of the Registry handout. ~45s.
